name: Bharwa Parwal with Tofu-Besan Filling
ingredients: 400 g small parwal (pointed gourd), washed and trimmed
150 g extra-firm tofu, pressed and finely crumbled
1 tsp (5 ml) mustard or canola oil
Chilli and modest salt to taste
steps: Trim parwal and make a lengthwise slit without cutting through. Scoop out the soft centre and finely chop it; keep the shells intact.
Press tofu and crumble finely. Dry-roast besan in a small pan over low heat until nutty and just lightly coloured; cool.
Heat measured oil. Add cumin, onion and ginger; cook until softened.
Add chopped parwal centres, tofu, coriander, turmeric, amchur, garam masala and chilli. Cook 3–4 minutes.
Stir in roasted besan and 1–2 tbsp water to bind the filling. Cook until the mixture is cohesive, then cool slightly.
Fill each parwal shell loosely; do not pack too tightly. Arrange in a wide non-stick pan with 2 tbsp water.
Cover and cook over low heat 10–14 minutes, turning gently once or twice, until parwal is tender but not collapsing. Add a splash of water if the pan dries.
Uncover for the final 2 minutes to evaporate excess moisture. Finish with coriander and lemon.
note: A lighter, plant-protein filling for the familiar stuffed parwal technique. Besan and tofu both contribute protein, but besan also contributes carbohydrate. Serve with a modest whole-grain roti portion and a larger side of non-starchy vegetables. Vegan.
sourceReferences: Culinary reference for slitting, stuffing and covered-pan cooking of pointed gourd; this tofu-besan filling and measured oil are our adaptation.
Additional reference for the spice profile and slow covered cooking technique; recipe quantities and filling differ.
Ingredient nutrition reference; final values depend on tofu and besan brands.
